# bloxone_cdc_destination_splunk_clouds (Data Source)

Retrieves information about existing Splunk Cloud Destinations.

The Splunk Cloud Destination object sends Cloud Data Connector (CDC) flow data to Splunk Cloud.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Get CDC Splunk Cloud Destinations filtered by an attribute
data "bloxone_cdc_destination_splunk_clouds" "example_by_attribute" {
  filters = {
    name = "example_cdc_destination_splunk_cloud"
  }
}

# Get CDC Splunk Cloud Destinations filtered by tag
data "bloxone_cdc_destination_splunk_clouds" "example_by_tag" {
  tag_filters = {
    site = "Site A"
  }
}

# Get all CDC Splunk Cloud Destinations
data "bloxone_cdc_destination_splunk_clouds" "example_all" {}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `filters` (Map of String) Filter are used to return a more specific list of results. Filters can be used to match resources by specific attributes, e.g. name. If you specify multiple filters, the results returned will have only resources that match all the specified filters.
- `tag_filters` (Map of String) Tag Filters are used to return a more specific list of results filtered by tags. If you specify multiple filters, the results returned will have only resources that match all the specified filters.

### Read-Only

- `results` (Attributes List) The list of Splunk Cloud Destinations matching the specified filters. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--results))

<a id="nestedatt--results"></a>
### Nested Schema for `results`

Required:

- `address` (String) The FQDN or IP address and port of the Splunk Cloud indexer, e.g. `splunkcloud.example.com:9997`. Multiple indexers are separated by commas, e.g. `10.10.10.1:9997,10.10.10.2:9997`.
- `ca_certificate` (String, Sensitive) The CA certificate used to verify the Splunk Cloud indexer certificate, in PEM format.
- `certificate` (String, Sensitive) The Splunk forwarder certificate, in PEM format.
- `indexer_name` (String) The name of the Splunk Cloud index the data is sent to.
- `name` (String) The name of the Splunk Cloud destination.

Optional:

- `certificate_key_passphrase` (String, Sensitive) The passphrase of the Splunk forwarder certificate key.
- `config_filename` (String) The name of the Universal Forwarder Credentials file downloaded from Splunk Cloud. Required when _config_option_ is _IMPORT_.
- `config_option` (String) The way the Splunk Cloud connection is configured. Allowed values:

  * _DEFAULT_
  * _MANUAL_
  * _IMPORT_

Defaults to _DEFAULT_.

~> **Note:** With _IMPORT_, set the connection fields from the Universal Forwarder Credentials file downloaded from Splunk Cloud, and _config_filename_ to its name.
- `description` (String) The description of the Splunk Cloud destination. May contain 0 to 256 characters.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Indicates whether the Splunk Cloud destination is enabled. Defaults to _true_.
- `output_data_format` (String) The format of the data sent to Splunk Cloud. Allowed values:

  * _CSV_
  * _CIM_

Defaults to _CSV_.
- `tags` (Map of String) The tags for the Splunk Cloud destination.

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) Time when the object has been created.
- `id` (Number) The resource identifier.
- `insecure_mode` (Boolean) Indicates whether the Splunk Cloud indexer certificate is not verified. Always _false_: insecure mode is not supported for Splunk Cloud.
- `updated_at` (String) Time when the object has been updated. Equals to _created_at_ if not updated after creation.
